scope: Proposition 11.1 (Coordinate ideal visibility) of the manuscript “Cuntz comparison and Jiang–Su absorption” (preprints/Cuntz-comparison-and-Jiang-Su-absorption-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 291 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5cbeda4528e0e671), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed k ≥ 2 there is a c.p.c. order-zero map ν : Mk → Aω ∩ A′, represented by c.p.c. maps νn : Mk → A, with weights hν n = νn(1), such that the following holds. For every test (a, ε), put b = (a − ε/8)+, yν n = a1/2 g(hν n)2 a1/2 . There are integers La,ε,n ≥ 1 and an ω-large set Ea,ε on which [b] ≤ La,ε,n[(yν n − ε/20)+] in Cu(A). (11.2) The integers need not be bounded as n varies.
